sentences.text: Tilemsisuchus lavocati is the only known species in its genus, a member of the family Dyrosauridae within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
Eric Buffetaut first named this animal in 1979.
Fossil lower jaws of T. lavocati show bite marks interpreted as the result of interspecific fights.
Researchers suggest these bite marks relate to behaviors like territoriality, hierarchy, and mating rights seen in modern male crocodilians.
It lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian.
It is debated whether similar behaviors in Dyrosauridae and modern crocodilians indicate an ancient trait inherited from a common ancestor.
